analysis:
Both changed files are test-only Swift sources under libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests. QwenTensorParallelBatchDriverTests.swift adds a build-ahead mode to the Pair harness (ahead/aheadByRank, buildsAhead on the driver) and tests for build-ahead, EOS discard, owner stop, late credits, held-token bounds, failure draining, and wire-word integrity. QwenTensorParallelBatchSessionTests.swift adds an optional `kind` parameter to the Owned test helper plus two executor tests (submitDecode/readDecode equivalence against read-then-build, and EOS retirement after a built-ahead step). No production code, wire format, key handling, attestation, authorization, logging or network surface changes in the supplied units, so no new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption (TB-002, TB-007, A-001, T-008, T-010) is introduced by these files.

The tests do exercise security-relevant production behavior the PR presumably adds elsewhere: fail-closed on rank disagreement about build-ahead, a corrupted decision word failing both ranks, no publication past the owner's stop, no publication of a token held after a stop or cancel, lane retirement and host drain on failure, and rejection of an undeclared discarded forward in the schedule (QwenLayerStageGenerationSchedule.finish). These are positive checks for T-010 (cancellation/stop propagation) and for failing closed, but I cannot verify from this batch that the production driver, executor or schedule implementations actually enforce them. The next pass should check the non-test sources: whether the held-token drop on a stop answer and the discard-one-forward EOS path leak unpublished tokens or leave KV or lane resources (cf. T-028 residual GPU memory) unreleased, whether the decision-word check cannot be bypassed, and whether the build-ahead agreement is enforced in QwenTensorParallelBatchSettings.agreementFields. The prefix-cache threat T-041 is not touched. The patch excerpt for the driver test file is truncated, but the head text lines 498-947 were reviewed directly.
